newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Provinces seek Beijing help on grain problem - paper.
newsitem.headline: Provinces seek Beijing help on grain problem - paper.

text.p: China's provincial chiefs have sought financial help from the central government after grain farmers were hit hard by slipping prices and slow sales after a 1996 bumper harvest, a Hong Kong newspaper said on Thursday.

Provincial officials had gathered at the National People's Congress, China's parliament which is currently in session, to discuss provincial budgets strained by government grain purchasing programmes designed to support prices, the Chinese-language Apple Daily said.

The paper quoted Hunan governor Yang Zhengwu as saying the provincial government purchased more than 20 million tonnes of grain from farmers at rates above the market price in order to encourage continued grain production and help minimise losses.

But after the purchase, the Hunan government had neither enough warehouses to store the grain, nor was it able to sell it, causing heavy losses in the province's grain department, Yang was quoted as saying.
Yang said the central Chinese province had about 15 million tonnes of grain available and could not find buyers.

The governor of China's northern province of Jilin, Wang Yunkun, said the province produced 23 million tonnes of grain last year and the local government was forced to buy grain from farmers to stabilise prices, the newspaper reported.
But this strained the province's finances, he said.
The newspaper quoted an informed source as saying China's State Council had decided to speed up its plan to purchase 15 million tonnes of grains for storage.
